Tu Yi from Ant Group presents a paper on Visually-rich Document Understanding. The co-authors are algorithm engineers from Ant Group. The paper focuses on understanding forms, receipts, and posters. Pre-training techniques, especially self-supervised multi-modal models, have shown success in VrDU tasks. However, existing models face reading order issues. The paper proposes LayoutMask, a novel pre-trained model. It uses text and layout information, enhancing text layout interactions and representations. LayoutMask differs from previous studies in 1D position choice, masking strategy, and pre-training objectives. It uses local 1D position instead of global 1D position. Two novel masking strategies, Whole Word Masking and Layout-Aware Masking, are introduced. A new pre-training objective, Masked Position Modeling, is also designed. Experiments show that Local-1D outperforms Global-1D on FUNSD and SROIE datasets, especially for the entity "Total". For more details, refer to the paper and posters.

Daniel Rotem presents work on adaptive inference in low resource settings. He discusses Multi Model and Early Exit methods. Multi Model is versatile but expensive to store and has overhead. Early Exit is memory efficient but can suffer from conflicting gradients. The study compares Multi Model and Early Exit classifiers on BERT pre-trained models. SWEET, a novel fine-tuning method for Early Exit, is introduced to avoid conflicting gradients. SWEET closes the gap between Early Exit and Multi Model but can negatively affect later classifiers. It outperforms both methods in fast speeds. The work shows conflicting gradients in Early Exit training and conducts a fair comparison of methods. SWEET motivates future research on Early Exit fine-tuning.

Multimodal relation extraction aims to determine semantic relations between entities in various forms. However, in realistic scenarios like social media, data is often multimodal. This work introduces a framework for multimodal relation extraction. It addresses internal-information over-utilization and external-information under-exploitation. A Graph Information Bottleneck principle - guided feature refinement is proposed. The framework consists of representing text and image with scene graphs, merging them into a unified backbone cross - modal graph, CMG. Then, CMG is screened and enriched with multimodal topic features. Experiments on a widely used MRE dataset show that leveraging visual features improves performance compared to text - based methods. The ablation study reveals that information screening and compensating contribute to task performance. The scene graph is beneficial for structural modeling of multimodal inputs. This work introduces a novel idea of simultaneous information subtraction and addition for multimodal relation extraction, achieving significant improvements over existing models.

Zhang Qin, Shenzhen University, presents "A Survey for Efficient Open Domain Question Answering" at ACL 2023. The work focuses on open-domain question answering, using a two-stage model with a question encoder and document encoder for retrieval. Challenges include large Wikipedia corpus, slow index file search, and multiple language models. Motivation is to achieve efficient systems with smaller memory, faster inference, and comparable performance. Core techniques include approximate nearest neighbor search, skip reading, and index size reduction. Conclusions suggest index size reduction for limited resources, model size reduction for trade-offs, and retrieval-only systems for real-time feedback. Future works include low-power device deployment and more evaluation metrics.

Text image modeling has advanced in quality but struggles with text representation. The Imagen model uses T5-XXL for text encoding. T5 uses SentencePiece, which tokenizes words into subwords. This makes it hard for the model to spell words correctly. Experiments show T5 has low spelling accuracy, while larger PaLM models perform better but are impractical. ByT5, which uses character-level information, spells well. T5 struggles with frequent words due to SentencePiece. Concatenating ByT5's text representation to Imagen improves spelling but not perfect. The main takeaways are the WikiSpell benchmark, DrawText benchmark, and a strategy to improve spelling by adding ByT5's representation.

This paper introduces LLM-Blender, an ensemble learning framework for large language models. It focuses on pairwise ranking and generative fusion. The team from AI2 and USC presents a two-stage framework. In the first stage, n models are run on an input X, and PairRanker compares the candidates. It encodes pairs of candidates with the input for better analysis. The top K candidates are then used in a sequence-to-sequence model for fusion. The PairRanker is different from prior methods as it compares candidates pairwise. Experiments show Blender outperforms other models on various metrics. The paper also presents MixInstruct, a dataset for evaluating large language models. LLM-Blender is simple yet effective, improving performance significantly.

Abstract: Marcos Treviso et al. introduce CREST, a joint framework for rationalization and counterfactual text generation. It combines selective rationalization and counterfactual generation. The rationalizer model generates rationales and counterfactuals. For evaluation, human evaluation on IMDB and SNLI shows CREST's counterfactuals are more valid and natural than MiCE. CREST can be used for data augmentation and rationalization with both factual and counterfactual examples. Experiments on IMDB, contrastive datasets, and out-of-domain datasets show CREST-Rationalization's superiority. CREST-Rationalization produces more plausible rationales and higher counterfactual simulability. CREST aims to produce valid, fluent, and diverse counterfactuals in a controllable way.

The paper presents a solution for multilingual machine translation called Language-Specific Layers, LSLs. It aims to increase capacity per language while keeping inference costs constant. LSLs use one regular transformer layer per language. At inference time, only the relevant sublayer is called. The paper explores LSL placement in the encoder. It uses a large model to learn the best placement of LSLs. The approach that performed best was to select the component based on the largest weight. The experiments were conducted on WMT21 news translation data for 10 languages, including low-resource languages. The learned architecture outperforms the baseline model and language adapters, especially for low-resource languages. The improvements are statistically significant for most translation directions.

The presentation introduces DrBERT, a French biomedical and clinical domain model based on RoBERTa and trained on NACHOS. It compares DrBERT with ChuBERT, trained on anonymized data from Nantes University Hospital. DrBERT outperforms CamemBERT on nine tasks. All NACHOS - based models are freely available on Hugging Face.

This paper presents a systematic study of knowledge distillation for natural language generation, NLG, with pseudo-target training. It aims to compress large NLG models while preserving performance. The study explores two main types of noise distillation: word - level and sequence - level. It contrasts with previous works focusing on classification or pre - training tasks. The study considers five realistic setups with medium - resource labeled data, large unlabeled data, medium - sized models, high compression rate, and negligible training resources. Four NLG tasks are studied: summarization, question generation, common sense reasoning, and simplification and style transfer. The paper explores extensions of pseudo - target usage, showing the importance of unlabeled data, generating multiple pseudo - targets, and proposing a novel joint - teaching technique. This paper introduces Dense-ATOMIC, a densely-connected commonsense knowledge graph. It aims to improve ATOMIC, a large commonsense knowledge base, by adding missing links like B-to-B, A-to-B, and A-to-A. Dense-ATOMIC has more multi-hop paths, enhancing knowledge coverage. A new CSKG completion method, Rel-CSKGC, is proposed. It uses RoBERTa for encoding and MaxPooling for link prediction. This method avoids sparse graph structure issues and utilizes semantic information. Evaluation shows Dense-ATOMIC outperforms ATOMIC in knowledge coverage and multi-hop paths. It also benefits commonsense reasoning tasks. The paper provides code and a website for further exploration.

Abstract: Zheng Yandan, Hao Anran and Luu Anh Tuan present Jointprop, a joint semi-supervised learning framework for name entity recognition, NER, and relation extraction, RE. They address the lack of interconnections between NER and RE tasks in existing studies. Their framework uses heterogeneous graphs to propagate labels across labeled and unlabeled data. It includes span feature generation, graph construction, joint label propagation, and model optimization. Experiments on four datasets show that Jointprop outperforms baselines on joint and single-task datasets, benefiting from task codependency in joint datasets.

This paper presents a novel framework, ULRA, for unsupervised automated essay scoring. It aims to overcome the limitations of previous works by introducing multiple heuristic quality signals as pseudo-groundtruth. ULRA includes a heuristic essay ranking module, HER alpha-shot, which generates partial order pairs based on different quality signals. A Deep Pairwise Rank Aggregation Module, DPRA, then aggregates these pairs for model training. A deep pairwise rank aggregation loss is designed to handle signal conflicts. In experiments, ULRA outperforms unsupervised baselines and achieves competitive performance with supervised methods. It effectively aggregates partial-order knowledge for unsupervised essay scoring.

Abstract: Dynamic networks can change architecture or parameters based on input, unlike static networks. However, fully dynamic networks use excessive parameters. This paper proposes PAD-Net, a partially dynamic network framework. It partitions parameters into dynamic and static, with scale factors for each. The Iterative Mode Partition method is used. Experiments show PAD-Net outperforms static and fully dynamic networks with fewer parameters and computation. Ablation studies find optimal Dynamic Ratios. Scale Factors are crucial for accuracy. Compared to network pruning, PAD-Net performs better. It makes output more discriminating. Future work includes extending to other networks, hardware - friendly methods, and more modes.

Abstract: Jingwei Yi from the University of Science and Technology of China presents a short advertisement video of their paper on protecting the copyright of embedding as services via backdoor watermark. The background of embedding as services is introduced, highlighting the exceptional capabilities of large language models like GPT, LLAMA, and PALM. The necessity to protect the copyright of embedding as services due to the risk of attackers stealing the model through learning from the embedding is emphasized. The paper proposes Embedding marker, a backdoor based watermark method applicable to embedding as services. It consists of two main steps: watermark injection and copyright verification. In watermark injection, a target embedding is defined, and the provided embedding is a weight summation of the target and original embeddings. Copyright verification involves constructing a back door and benign data set, and computing similarities between requested embeddings and the target embedding. Experiments on four data sets show great detection performance and utility for downstream tasks. The covertness of the provided embedding is also validated.

PromptRank ist ein data-effizienter Ansatz für Multi-hop QA. Es kombiniert eine unüberwachte Retrieval-Methode mit einem few-shot Sprachmodell-basierten Reranker. Zuerst werden Kandidatenketten mit TF-IDF und Hyperlink-Traversal ermittelt. Diese werden dann mit einem few-shot Sprachmodell reranked. Der Likelihood des Fragen-gegeben-Kette-Prompts wird verwendet. PromptRank übertrifft vollständig überwachte Systeme wie DrKit und zeigt vergleichbare Leistung zu state-of-the-art Multi-hop-dichten Retrievers. Es verwendet nur 128 Beispiele und ist data-effizient. PromptRank ist für Multi-hop QA in der Downstream-Performance sehr gut. Es ist ein starkes Few-shot Path Retrieval-System im Vergleich zu vollständig überwachten Systemen. Die Likelihood-Funktion funktioniert wesentlich besser als die umgekehrte. The paper presents QUEST, a retrieval dataset for studying selective information needs. It includes over 3, 000 queries with implicit set constraints. Examples like Jane's search for a Costa Rican reptile and Austin's preference for French historical fiction are used. QUEST is constructed using Wikipedia categories and verified by human annotators. It shows a challenging retrieval problem due to multi-answer sets and evidence from different document parts. Baselines like retrievers and a T5-based reranker are considered. Results indicate room for improvement in retriever performance and end - to - end system F1 scores. Set intersection and difference queries are particularly difficult. QUEST aims to help researchers build better systems for selective information - seeking scenarios.

The work revisits the minimal pair paradigm for evaluating language models' acceptability judgments. It addresses the lack of robustness of current methods to context length. The authors create longer sequences by adding acceptable or unacceptable sentences from datasets like BLiMP and SyntaxGym as prefixes. They find that MPP judgments are mostly robust for unrelated context, but vary significantly when prefixes are from the same dataset. This shows models' sensitivity to shared syntactic and semantic features. The study suggests that current MPP evaluation may not fully capture models' knowledge across context windows. Unnatural Instructions ist ein Dataset für eine Vielzahl von natürlichen Sprachaufgaben. Es enthält 64.000 Beispiele, von denen es durch Paraphrasen auf etwa 240.000 Beispiele erweitert werden kann. Die generierten Beispiele sind kreativ und vielfältig, und mehr als 50% sind korrekt. Ein 11 Milliarden Parameter großer T5-Modell wird auf Unnatural Instructions finetuned und übertrifft sowohl T0++ als auch Tk-instruct auf mehreren Benchmarks. Unnatural Instructions zeigt die Fähigkeit von Sprachmodellen, kreative und vielfältige Daten zu generieren, was mit Crowd Workers schwierig ist. The paper presents a study on improving pretraining techniques for code-switched NLP. It defines code-switching as the mixing of languages in a sentence, common in linguistically diverse communities like India. It points out that multilingual models like mBERT and XLM-R perform poorly on code-switched tasks. The main contributions are novel MLM techniques, SwitchMLM, and FrequencyMLM, which are tuned for code-switching. SwitchMLM focuses on masking switch-points, while FrequencyMLM uses negative log likelihood from monolingual corpora. Architectural modifications like residual connections are proposed to encode more switch-point information. The results show that the combined method performs best on sentiment analysis tasks. Probing experiments verify that the proposed methods increase switch-point information in intermediate and final layers. This leads to architectural changes and an auxiliary loss to further enhance switch-point information content.

Abstract: This research explores MultiInstruct, a multi-modal instruction tuning benchmark dataset. It aims to improve multi-modal zero-shot learning via instruction tuning. The dataset consists of 62 diverse tasks across 10 categories, derived from 21 datasets. OFA, a unified multi-modal pre-trained model, is used as the base. Training involves 53 tasks, testing uses 10, 000 instances per task. Experiments show that instruction tuning significantly improves OFA's performance on seen tasks. They propose a training strategy with Temporal span extraction pre-training and time-sensitive reinforcement learning. Their TempT5 model outperforms others in OBQA and Reasoning QA. The paper introduces a method to transfer reasoning abilities from large language models to much smaller ones. It proposes using large models as reasoning teachers and a novel technique called diverse reasoning. The method involves applying chain - of - thought prompting on large models to generate step - by - step solutions, which are then used to fine - tune smaller models. Diverse reasoning is emphasized as a key technique, generating multiple solutions using stochastic temperature sampling. Experiments show that the method can achieve notable performance on various tasks, especially text - based ones, and outperforms vanilla fine - tuning. The method is highly scalable but involves trade - offs between development and inference costs. The paper provides details on reasoning emergence in small models and results on open - source models. The authors evaluate the data set with human participants and established models. Results show that without task-specific training, models perform poorly. However, with training on KITMUS, some models improve significantly. The study highlights that many models struggle with integrating backward knowledge presented only at inference time. Dialogue summarization aims to distill salient information from a dialogue context into a concise summary. This is a challenging task in text summarization. Existing methods mainly focus on pre-computed static graph structures, but they have drawbacks like relying on unreliable external tools and not being able to adapt dynamically. The SDDS model proposed here has four main components. It uses an Utterance Encoder to vectorize utterances. A Static-Dynamic Graph module combines static and dynamic graphs to capture semantic relationships. A pre-trained language model generates the final summary. The model structures are detailed. Four heuristic methods are used for static structure modeling. A sliding window method is proposed for speaker interaction. Relative distance is used for utterance position graph. A Dynamic Graph module uses multi-head attention for semantic relationship capture. A fusion method combines static and dynamic graphs. A dual cross-attention mechanism is used to incorporate graph representation in the generation process. The code and data are available on GitHub.

Abstract: This work introduces the Dual Cache for Long Document Neural Coreference Resolution. Coreference resolution aims to link mentions referring to the same entity. Conventional methods have quadratic complexity. Cache-based methods use a fixed-size cache, reducing complexity to linear. However, LRU eviction policy in long documents leads to high cache misses for high-frequency entities. A dual cache is proposed, with a local cache using LRU and a global cache using LFU. The model scans the document, classifying mentions and evaluating their frequency. Dual cache outperforms single cache methods on benchmarks and reduces cache misses significantly. It has the highest performance/cost ratio compared to single cache methods.

The paper presents an approach to abductive reasoning without supervision. It starts with a context and an outcome, then explores possible explanations. The work introduces a Neural Divide-and-Conquer Reasoning Framework for image retrieval from linguistically complex text. It addresses the challenge of highly similar images and long descriptions. Inspired by Divide-and-Conquer and Dual-Process Theory, it proposes a method combining System 1 and System 2. The first model, Proposition Generator, decomposes complex text into simple propositions. Visual-Linguistic Interactor performs visual-proposition interaction. Neural-Symbolic Reasoner integrates reasoning states and results. Combining System 1 and System 2 inference results yields the final solution. Experimental results show NDCR outperforms baselines. The method is interoperable and effective for complex reasoning. Suggestions include exploring neural symbolic calculation for compositional reasoning and integrating Dual-Process Theory with Divide-and-Conquer.

This paper discusses the dependency structure of coordination. It contrasts asymmetric approaches, like universal dependencies and Igor Mel'čuk's theory, where the first conjunct is the head, with symmetric approaches. It argues for symmetric structures based on the principle of dependency length minimization. Examples show that shorter dependencies are preferred. Statistics from the Penn Treebank confirm that left conjuncts tend to be shorter when the governor is on the left or absent. This tendency disappears when the governor is on the right. The paper provides arguments against asymmetric structures and for symmetric ones.

Grounded language understanding is lacking in current language models. It involves mapping natural language expressions to executable plans or programs in specific environments. Challenges include pre-training without grounding. Existing research often uses language models for direct plan generation, which may not always be grammatical or valid. A novel framework, Pangu, is proposed. It focuses on discrimination, where a symbolic agent proposes plans and a language model scores and ranks them. This avoids the need for the language model to handle plan validity. Pangu shows strong performance across different language models and settings, including fine-tuning and in-context learning. It demonstrates good sample efficiency and robustness under non-i.i.d. settings. The key takeaway is that discrimination might be a better strategy for grounded language understanding than generation.

This work presents a two-step pipeline for finding high-agreement Amazon Mechanical Turk, MTurk, Workers for summarization. It starts with qualification settings, including pre-task qualifications like location, number of HITs, and HIT Approval Rate. The first qualification task tests annotators' ability to evaluate multiple dimensions correctly, categorizing them into gold, silver, bronze, and block. Only gold and silver workers pass. The second endurance task assesses capacity for handling heavy workload. Reference-based tasks test general performance. Baseline MTurk workers are compared using MACE, while CloudResearch MTurk workers are also analyzed. Across annotation sources, Pipeline and CloudResearch workers show significant Spearman's correlation. The pipeline results in 6% of 200 participants achieving high agreement at a lower cost, serving as a best practice for high-agreement annotations. Future work includes investigating high-quality worker hiring and trying multiple applications. Limitations include only English summarization on MTurk and no guarantee of correctness training.

The work presents U-CREAT, a method for unsupervised case retrieval in the legal domain. It addresses the challenge of retrieving relevant cited documents from a large pool of cases. The IL-PCR dataset is introduced as a benchmark for prior case retrieval tasks, containing 7,070 legal cases with an average of 6.775 citations per query. The U-CREAT pipeline uses unsupervised learning and an event-based approach. Event extraction is crucial, using dependency parsing and focusing on verb categories. The pipeline processes query and candidate documents, computes an interaction matrix, and ranks candidates. Experiments with various models show that event-based models, especially Event Filtered Documents, outperform others in terms of performance, inference time, and F1 scores. U-CREAT is the current state-of-the-art method for the COLIEE’21 document retrieval task. It opens new avenues for prior case retrieval research.

Results on the eRisk datasets show DisorBERT's good balance in precision and recall. Examples demonstrate DisorBERT's focus on mental disorder-related words. Abstract: This research presents a document - level relation extraction framework with uncertainty - guided label denoising. It aims to improve the label quality of distantly supervised data. A pre - denoising DocRE model is trained with both DS and human - annotated data to generate pseudo labels. Uncertainty estimation is introduced to determine model prediction trustworthiness. An instance - level uncertainty estimation method is proposed for overlapping relations. A re - labeling strategy with dynamic class uncertainty thresholds is designed. A multi - phase training strategy is also developed to iteratively re - label DS data. The framework outperforms several strong baselines on public datasets. The main contributions include the uncertainty - guided label denoising framework, instance - level uncertainty estimation for overlapping relations, iterative re - labeling strategy with dynamic class uncertainty thresholds, and great performance improvements.

The paper discusses using large language models for evaluating text quality in natural language processing as an alternative to human evaluation. It proposes instructing large language models with natural language instructions to rate samples based on attributes like grammar, coherence, likability, and relevance. The paper also addresses potential questions about agreement between large language models and human evaluators, the impact of instruction wordings and sampling methods, and the benefits and costs of using large language model evaluation compared to human evaluation. Multilingual Sprachmodelle wie Codex und BLOOM sind für multilinguale semantische Parsing Aufgaben noch unzureichend. This work investigates label bias problems in in-context learning for large language models. It starts by defining a typology of label biases, identifying domain-label bias as a new type. Experiments show that random in-domain words from the task corpus can bias model predictions, while random English words do not. To mitigate biases, a domain-context calibration method is proposed. It uses random in-domain words to estimate and correct bias, outperforming previous calibration methods. Experiments on various models and datasets confirm significant improvements in in-context learning performance, especially on tasks with large domain-label bias. This work provides a systematic approach to handling label biases in in-context learning.

The meta-mapper network maps visual concepts into a unified audio semantic space. The encoder and generator use a transformer-based approach with an alpha to evaluate modality contributions. Dual Counterfactual Contrastive Learning optimizes visual-textual alignment. Experiments on MSVD and MSR-VTT benchmarks show TAVT outperforms SOTA models, especially in low-resource domains. The task of emotion regulation in conversations aims to predict the emotion label of each utterance. Existing methods focus on speaker and contextual information but face challenges like underexploiting multimodal information complementarity, unsatisfactory performance in minority emotion classes, and difficulty distinguishing semantically similar emotions. This paper proposes MultiEMO, an attention - based correlation - aware multimodal fusion framework. It includes VisExtNet for visual feature extraction, MultiAttn for multimodal fusion, and Sample - Weighted Focal Contrast loss for emotion classification. VisExtNet captures facial expressions without redundant scene - related information. MultiAttn integrates textual, audio, and visual modalities through cross - attention. SWFC loss enhances classification of minority and semantically similar emotions. Extensive experiments on MELD and IEMOCAP show state - of - the - art performance. Limitations include VisExtNet's inability to distinguish speakers and irrelevant people, SWFC loss's requirement for large batch size on MELD, and worse performance in minority emotions compared to majority classes.

The paper presents FSUIE, a novel fuzzy span mechanism for enhancing universal information extraction. It addresses the overreliance on precise span boundaries in current span - based UIE models and the mismatch between transformer feature extraction and information extraction. FSUIE proposes a fuzzy span attention to adaptively adjust the attention span of the model, which represents the target boundary as a continuous distribution of correct probability. It also introduces a fuzzy span loss to alleviate the model's reliance on span boundaries. Experiments on named entity recognition, relationship extraction, and aspect sentiment triplet extraction show that FSUIE achieves significant performance improvements and new state - of - the - art results. The ablation study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed mechanisms. Overall, FSUIE achieves excellent results in a wide range of information extraction tasks.

Abstract: This work presents a critical look at weakly supervised learning, WSL. It introduces weak supervision and weakly supervised learning. In WSL, data is labeled using weak sources, which are cheaper but noisy. Direct training on weakly labeled data leads to memorization of noise. Recent WSL methods claim high performance on clean test sets but often assume access to a clean validation set. This research addresses whether clean validation data is necessary. It finds that clean validation samples are crucial for proper WSL. Increasing clean validation samples improves performance. Direct fine-tuning on clean data outperforms WSL approaches. Yujie Wang from Shanxi University presents a paper on "Dynamic Heterogeneous-Graph Reasoning with Language Models and Knowledge Representation Learning for Commonsense QA". This task is challenging as it demands machines to answer questions relying on common knowledge, testing their language understanding. Knowledge is stored in language models and knowledge bases. Previous works combine these to solve Commonsense QA but introduce noisy entities and limit interaction between modalities. DHLK is proposed. It builds an HKG based on multiple knowledge bases using a two-stage pruning strategy and KRL. It encodes and fuses QA contexts and entities using RoBERTa and Mask Self-Attention. It dynamically removes weakly relevant entities. Entity and relation embeddings are optimized using TransE. Relation Mask Self-Attention is introduced to model subgraphs. The HKG graph embedding is obtained by max-pooling. HKG path information is incorporated into QA context. The final answer prediction uses HKG graph embedding, paths, and QA context embedding in an MLP. Experiments on CommonsenseQA and OpenBookQA show good results compared to other methods.

Xiao Xu, a third-year PhD student from Harbin Institute of Technology, presents "ManagerTower: Aggregating the Insights of Uni-Modal Experts for Vision-Language Representation Learning" at ACL 2023. This work, done during an internship in the MSRIC group with Intel Cognitive Computing Group support, aims to train a smart AI system understanding both images and text. Vision-Language learning focuses on Visual Question Answering, where models need to answer questions based on images. Recent progress in transformer-based models has been remarkable since 2019, thanks to large-scale self-supervised pre-training on image-text pairs. The work proposes ManagerTower, a novel VL modal architecture. It uses RoBERTa and CLIP-ViT base as unimodal encoders. ManagerTower introduces managers in each cross-modal layer to gather insights from pre-trained unimodal experts at different levels. This allows for adaptive exploitation of different levels of unimodal semantic knowledge, improving cross-modal alignment and fusion. The work introduces INK, a framework for injecting kNN knowledge into nearest neighbor machine translation. It aims to improve NMT model generalization and performance. The core idea is to smooth predictions based on nearest neighbors in the representation space. The framework has two steps: extracting kNN knowledge to guide adapter adjustment and updating representations asynchronously. It optimizes the adapter with a combined learning objective. Experiments show INK outperforms state-of-the-art kNN-MT systems, achieving higher BLEU scores with less memory and faster inference. It also explores how kNN knowledge affects representation distribution and adapter-datastore combination. Overall, INK enhances NMT model representation space and translation performance.

Abstract: This work presents a graph-based approach for out-of-vocabulary, OOV, word embedding learning. It focuses on handling OOV words by observing their word formation and associating them with relevant words. A Word Relationship Graph is introduced, mimicking lexical rules. The OOV word is tokenized and associated with other words, forming a two-level graph. A self-attention network assigns attributes to OOV nodes. Graph Attention Networks are used to extract important information. A readout block layer summarizes word formation. Contrastive learning with NT-XENT is applied in the loss function. Extensive experiments show the model's superiority over baselines. The model benefits static and contextual models in downstream tasks. Agglutinative languages are well-suited, while fusional languages present more challenges. The model's performance with English is good through reasonable word segmentation. The graph in the model can handle various complex word formations. The application to other languages depends on rational word decomposition.

The study finds that human explanations can still benefit model predictions even if considered low quality by humans. The TREU metric outperforms the simulatability score in evaluating the helpfulness of human explanations. The research lays the foundation for high - quality human collaboration in annotation jobs.

Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for compositional generalization in semantic parsing without using trees. It introduces a neural seq2seq model that directly models correspondences between input and output fragments. The model tags each input token with an unordered multiset of output tokens and then uses another model to predict a permutation for the output. This approach avoids the need for trees, which are usually computationally expensive to obtain. The model outperforms other treeless models on the COGS benchmark, especially in generalization to deeper recursion. It addresses challenges like alignment between input and output and finding linguistically plausible permutations. The permutation method is flexible but NP-hard, so a GPU - friendly continuous relaxation is used for approximation.

The paper presents an investigation into superhuman performance in NLU. It discusses how leaderboard-based evaluation has become standard, leading to systems achieving human or even superhuman performance in benchmarks. These benchmarks are called "saturated benchmarks". The paper analyzes SuperGLUE and SQuAD benchmarks. It finds that humans are outperformed by systems on most tasks. However, there are errors in the datasets and ground - truth answers that make the comparison unfair. The paper argues that researchers often vaguely estimate human performance and that pay rates for humans vary, affecting the quality of the results. It concludes that claims of superhuman performance are not yet grounded and provides recommendations to avoid mistakes and construct more reliable benchmarks.

The paper investigates the generalization of CoNLL-2003 named entity taggers in 2023. It observes that these models have been used for almost 20 years and raises questions about their generalization to modern data and factors for good generalization. The CoNLL++ dataset, a collection of Reuters News from 2020 annotated with CoNLL-2003 guidelines, is developed. Over 20 models are fine - tuned on CoNLL-03 and CoNLL++. Good generalization requires a better model architecture, larger model size, and more fine - tuning examples. The performance drop is mainly caused by temporal drift, not adaptive overfitting. The conclusion is that CoNLL-2003 taggers still work well in 2023. The paper calls for more research on improving model generalization.

The paper "Python Code Generation by Asking Clarification Questions" addresses the challenge of input underspecification in code generation. It proposes interactivity through clarification questions to gather more specifications. A method to create CodeClarQA, a synthetic dataset with clarifications on key operations, is introduced. The pipeline includes a Clarification Need Predictor, Question Selector, and Code Generator. The paper shows good performance in identifying missing key operations, with MPNet performing best. Error analysis reveals challenges like taxonomy and argument. The CQ-driven code generation pipeline is tested, showing improvements with more high-ranked CQs answered. However, it underperforms the model-only trainer. Clarified key operations contribute to better generated code, but the task remains challenging.

Armineh Nourbakhsh, a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon University and research director at JP Morgan AI Research, presents "CounterComp". This work focuses on using counterfactual scenarios to enhance compositional generalization for multi - step quantitative reasoning in question - answering tasks. It addresses the limitation of state - of - the - art neural models in handling multi - step operations due to memorizing spurious patterns. CounterComp mines counterfactual scenarios from training samples to create positive and negative examples. These are used to add an auxiliary metric learning loss to the training procedure, which improves model performance, especially with increasing reasoning steps. This loss also helps the model attend to more meaningful tokens during training. The work shows consistent performance improvement on in - and out - of - distribution samples, demonstrating its effectiveness in compositional generalization.
